claim: A cDNA kinase screen was performed by co-expressing Wnt8a-GFP and membrane-bound mCherry in PAC2 cells together with 229 kinases from a Medaka cDNA library.
source: To identify potential cytoneme regulators, we performed a cell-culture-based genetic screen (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–J) by co-expressing Wnt8a-GFP and glycophosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored, membrane-bound mCherry (memCherry) in PAC2 cells together with arrayed cDNA clones from a Medaka cDNA library consisting of 229 kinases (Chen et al., 2014; Souren et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental procedure of the screen, including the number of kinases tested and the cell type used.

claim: Ror2 was identified as a kinase that stimulates both filopodia number per cell and average filopodia length above the 85th percentile.
source: The tyrosine-protein kinase transmembrane receptor Ror2 was found to stimulate both filopodia number per cell as well as average filopodia length above the 85th percentile (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from the screen shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Ror2 expression significantly increased the average number and length of filopodia per cell in PAC2 fibroblasts.
source: Ror2 expression significantly increased the average number and length of filopodia per cell (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1F and supplementary figures.

claim: Ror2 requires homodimerization for transautophosphorylation and subsequent downstream signaling.
source: Ror2 requires homodimerization for transautophosphorylation and subsequent downstream signaling (Liu et al., 2007), which can be inhibited by overexpressing a kinase-dead construct.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2007.

claim: Transfection of the dominant-negative mutant Ror23I caused a reduction in both the number of protrusions and their average length.
source: Transfection of the dominant-negative mutant Ror23I (Hikasa et al., 2002) caused a reduction in both the number of protrusions and their average length, consistent with an essential role of the Ror2 kinase activity in filopodia induction in PAC2 fibroblasts.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Hikasa et al., 2002.

claim: Cdc42 is crucial for organizing the actin cytoskeleton to stabilize Wnt cytonemes.
source: The Rho GTPase Cdc42 is crucial for organizing the actin cytoskeleton to stabilize Wnt cytonemes (Stanganello et al., 2015) and is thought to be a downstream target of the Wnt/Ror2 pathway regulating filopodia (Schambony and Wedlich, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Blockage of Cdc42 function by co-transfection with dominant-negative Cdc42T17N reduced filopodia formation significantly.
source: To determine whether Ror2-induced filopodia require Cdc42 function in order to assemble an actin scaffold we co-transfected Ror2-stimulated fibroblasts with dominant-negative Cdc42T17N (Nalbant et al., 2004). Blockage of Cdc42 function reduced filopodia formation significantly (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F and a citation to Nalbant et al., 2004.

claim: IRSp534k expression blocks Ror2-induced filopodia formation.
source: IRSp534k expression, like Cdc42T17N transfection, blocks Ror2-induced filopodia formation (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: Treatment of Ror2-expressing cells with ML141, a GTPase inhibitor for Cdc42/Rac1, caused a substantial reduction in both the number and the length of filopodia.
source: Treatment of Ror2-expressing cells with ML141, a GTPase inhibitor for Cdc42/Rac1 (Surviladze et al., 2010), also caused a substantial reduction in both the number and the length of filopodia.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Surviladze et al., 2010.

claim: Ror2 is a crucial regulator of filopodia in PAC2 fibroblasts.
source: Thus, Ror2 is a crucial regulator of filopodia in PAC2 fibroblasts, and filopodia depend on a Cdc42-mediated actin scaffold for their outgrowth and maintenance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Filopodia depend on a Cdc42-mediated actin scaffold for their outgrowth and maintenance.
source: Thus, Ror2 is a crucial regulator of filopodia in PAC2 fibroblasts, and filopodia depend on a Cdc42-mediated actin scaffold for their outgrowth and maintenance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ror2 is a member of the family of orphan receptor tyrosine kinases, possessing an extracellular Fzd-like CRD, a cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase domain, and a proline-rich domain (PRD).
source: Ror2 is a member of the family of orphan receptor tyrosine kinases, possessing an extracellular Fzd-like CRD, a cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase domain, and a proline-rich domain (PRD) (Yoda et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yoda et al., 2003.

claim: Ror2 binds Wnt5a via its extracellular cysteine-rich domain (CRD).
source: Ror2 is a tyrosine kinase receptor that binds Wnt5a via its extracellular cysteine-rich domain (CRD) (Hikasa et al., 2002) and serves as a β-catenin independent Wnt co-receptor activating the PCP signaling pathway (Schambony and Wedlich, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hikasa et al., 2002.

claim: Ror2 serves as a β-catenin independent Wnt co-receptor activating the PCP signaling pathway.
source: Ror2 is a tyrosine kinase receptor that binds Wnt5a via its extracellular cysteine-rich domain (CRD) (Hikasa et al., 2002) and serves as a β-catenin independent Wnt co-receptor activating the PCP signaling pathway (Schambony and Wedlich, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Schambony and Wedlich, 2007.

claim: Zebrafish ror2 is expressed ubiquitously in early development, with its expression peaking during gastrulation between 2 and 9 hours post fertilization (hpf).
source: Zebrafish ror2 is expressed ubiquitously in early development, with its expression peaking during gastrulation between 2 and 9 hours post fertilization (hpf) (Bai et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bai et al., 2014.

claim: Expression of the β-catenin Wnt ligand wnt8a is confined to the embryonic margin during zebrafish gastrulation, orchestrating patterning of the prospective neural plate.
source: Expression of the β-catenin Wnt ligand wnt8a is confined to the embryonic margin during zebrafish gastrulation, orchestrating patterning of the prospective neural plate (Kelly et al., 1995; Rhinn et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kelly et al., 1995 and Rhinn et al., 2005.

claim: Wnt8a-GFP displays a punctate pattern in the cytoplasm and at the membrane, including cytoneme tips.
source: Confocal microscopy on live specimens revealed that Wnt8a-GFP displays a punctate pattern in the cytoplasm and at the membrane, including cytoneme tips, but when Wnt is absent, Ror2-mCherry is uniformly distributed in the cell membrane (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: When Wnt is absent, Ror2-mCherry is uniformly distributed in the cell membrane.
source: Confocal microscopy on live specimens revealed that Wnt8a-GFP displays a punctate pattern in the cytoplasm and at the membrane, including cytoneme tips, but when Wnt is absent, Ror2-mCherry is uniformly distributed in the cell membrane (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: When Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry are co-expressed in the same cell, Ror2-mCherry accumulates in punctae along the membrane.
source: When Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry are co-expressed in the same cell, Ror2-mCherry accumulates in punctae along the membrane (Figure 2A, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Correlated fluorescence intensity analysis of Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry suggests that both proteins predominantly co-localize in membrane-associated clusters.
source: Correlated fluorescence intensity analysis of Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry suggests that both proteins predominantly co-localize in membrane-associated clusters (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence intensity analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A Pearson-based correlation analysis of Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry in embryonic tissue of a volume of 40 × 40 × 60 µm3 supports co-localization.
source: This is supported by a Pearson-based correlation analysis of Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry in embryonic tissue of a volume of 40 × 40 × 60 µm3 (N=8, Supplementary Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pearson correlation analysis shown in Supplementary Figure 2G.

claim: A similar intensity correlation was found between Wnt5b and Ror2.
source: We found a similar intensity correlation between Wnt5b and Ror2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The CRD of Ror2 is crucial for interaction with Wnt ligands.
source: The CRD of Ror2 is crucial for interaction with Wnt ligands (Hikasa et al., 2002; Mikels et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hikasa et al., 2002 and Mikels et al., 2009.

claim: Ror2-ΔCRD-GFP still localizes to the cell membrane and with Wnt8a-mCherry forming clusters therein.
source: We observed that Ror2-ΔCRD-GFP still localizes to the cell membrane and with Wnt8a-mCherry forming clusters therein.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations described in the text.

claim: Image profile analysis showed a marked reduction of the intensity peaks at the cluster site for Ror2-ΔCRD, indicating that Ror2-CRD is required for the interaction with Wnt8a.
source: However, image profile analysis showed a marked reduction of the intensity peaks at the cluster site, indicating that Ror2-CRD is required for the interaction with Wnt8a (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by image profile analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Line-scanning fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (lsFCS) measures the concentrations and diffusion coefficients of ligands and receptors in the presence of a membrane.
source: We further characterized Wnt8a/Ror2 protein–protein interactions in vivo using line-scanning fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (lsFCS; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), which measures the concentrations and diffusion coefficients of ligands and receptors in the presence of a membrane (Dörlich et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dörlich et al., 2015.

claim: lsFCS analysis revealed a receptor concentration (area density) Cr=(37 ± 3) µm−2 for Ror2-mCherry in spot 1.
source: In spot 1, we found intensity fluctuation from Ror2-mCherry emission (Figure 2D). A fit of the autocorrelation function revealed a receptor concentration (area density) Cr=(37 ± 3) µm−2.
evidence: The claim is supported by lsFCS data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The diffusion coefficient of Ror2-mCherry in spot 1 is D=(0.28 ± 0.03) µm2 s−1, similar to values found for LRP6 receptors in the plasma membrane.
source: The diffusion coefficient, D=(0.28 ± 0.03) µm2 s−1, is similar to values found for LRP6 receptors in the plasma membrane (Dörlich et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by lsFCS data and a citation to Dörlich et al., 2015.

claim: There was no clear emission from Wnt8a-GFP molecules in spot 1.
source: There was no clear emission from Wnt8a-GFP molecules in spot 1.
evidence: The claim is based on lsFCS measurements described in the text.

claim: lsFCS on spot 2 revealed clear autocorrelations in both color channels, indicating the presence of both Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry at this site.
source: By contrast, lsFCS on spot 2 revealed clear autocorrelations in both color channels (Figure 2E), indicating the presence of both Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry at this site.
evidence: The claim is supported by lsFCS data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: A dual-color cross-correlation between Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry was found in spot 2, indicating concerted intensity fluctuations in both color channels, which arise from their co-diffusion in the plasma membrane due to binding.
source: We found a dual-color cross-correlation between Wnt8a-GFP and Ror2-mCherry (Figure 2E), indicating concerted intensity fluctuations in both color channels, which arise from their co-diffusion in the plasma membrane due to binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by lsFCS data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The cross-correlation lsFCS data provide clear evidence of complex formation between Wnt8a and Ror2.
source: Therefore, the cross-correlation lsFCS data provide clear evidence of complex formation between Wnt8a and Ror2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lsFCS data.

claim: The low diffusion coefficient of the bound species, D=(0.02 ± 0.01) µm2 s−1, indicates that the complexes diffuse as large clusters.
source: Furthermore, the low diffusion coefficient of the bound species, D=(0.02 ± 0.01) µm2 s−1, indicates that the complexes diffuse as large clusters.
evidence: The claim is based on lsFCS measurements and interpretation of the diffusion coefficient.

claim: Fzd7 interacts with Ror2 and enhances Ror2-mediated signaling during Xenopus gastrulation.
source: We have previously shown that Fzd7 also interacts with Ror2 and enhances Ror2-mediated signaling during Xenopus gastrulation (Brinkmann et al., 2016), suggesting that Fzd7a could be a part of the Wnt8a/Ror2 cluster in zebrafish.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Brinkmann et al., 2016.

claim: Overexpression of Ror2-mCherry, Fzd7a-CFP and Wnt8a-GFP showed co-localization of all three proteins in the cell membrane.
source: To test this, we overexpressed Ror2-mCherry, Fzd7a-CFP and Wnt8a-GFP and found co-localization of all three proteins in the cell membrane (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Wnt8a interacts with Ror2 by binding to its CRD.
source: From our data, we conclude that Wnt8a interacts with Ror2 by binding to its CRD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Wnt8a and Ror2 co-migrate and form dense protein clusters.
source: Wnt8a and Ror2 co-migrate and form dense protein clusters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Wnt8a/Ror2 clusters are in close steric contact with other components of the Wnt signaling complex including Fzd7a.
source: The data suggest that the Wnt8a/Ror2 clusters are in close steric contact with other components of the Wnt signaling complex including Fzd7a.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PCP signaling plays a role in regulating tissue migration during gastrulation.
source: PCP signaling plays a role in regulating tissue migration during gastrulation (Tada and Heisenberg, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tada and Heisenberg, 2012.

claim: PCP signaling via Ror2 activation regulates collective cell migration towards the embryonic midline, which is most pronounced in the mesodermal germ layer in zebrafish.
source: PCP signaling via Ror2 activation regulates collective cell migration towards the embryonic midline, which is most pronounced in the mesodermal germ layer in zebrafish (Bai et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bai et al., 2014.

claim: Overexpression of Ror2 receptor alone had a very small effect on the establishment of the ntl expression domain.
source: To this end, we overexpressed the Ror2 receptor, which alone had a very small effect on the establishment of the ntl expression domain (for classification see Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Overexpression of Wnt8a leads to a broadening and shortening of the ntl expression domain.
source: However, overexpression of Wnt8a leads to a broadening and shortening of the ntl expression domain.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations described in the text.

claim: A similar phenotype to Wnt8a overexpression was observed when Wnt8a and Ror2 were co-expressed.
source: A similar phenotype was observed when Wnt8a and Ror2 were co-expressed.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations described in the text.

claim: Categorization of the phenotypes suggests that the co-activation of Ror2/Wnt8a and Ror2/Wnt5b have similar effects.
source: Categorization of the phenotypes suggests that the co-activation of Ror2/Wnt8a and Ror2/Wnt5b have similar effects (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotype categorization shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Inhibition of Ror2 function by either Ror23I expression or a Morpholino-based Ror2 knock-down led to CE defects.
source: Inhibition of Ror2 function by either Ror23I expression or a Morpholino-based Ror2 knock-down also led to CE defects.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations described in the text.

claim: An enhanced broadening of the embryonic midline was found if Wnt8/Fzd7a and Wnt8a/Fzd7a/Ror2 were overexpressed.
source: We found an enhanced broadening of the embryonic midline if Wnt8/Fzd7a and Wnt8a/Fzd7a/Ror2 were overexpressed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Endogenous Ror2 is already expressed at high levels, and the available Wnt ligand concentration is the key quantity-controlling step for PCP signaling during zebrafish CE.
source: This suggests that endogenous Ror2 is already expressed at high levels, and that the available Wnt ligand concentration is the key quantity-controlling step for PCP signaling during zebrafish CE.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cells had a less bipolar shape and displayed a more circular form in embryos with Wnt8/Ror2 signaling, reminiscent of Ror2 activation by Wnt5a.
source: We found that the cells had a less bipolar shape and displayed a more circular form in embryos with Wnt8/Ror2 signaling, reminiscent of Ror2 activation by Wnt5a (Figure 3C,D), suggesting that mediolateral narrowing of axial mesoderm is reduced.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: During Xenopus gastrulation, Wnt5A activates Ror2 downstream signaling, leading to Cdc42 activation, JNK phosphorylation, and ultimately, the enhancement of ATF2 transcription.
source: During Xenopus gastrulation, Wnt5A activates Ror2 downstream signaling, leading to Cdc42 activation, JNK phosphorylation, and ultimately, the enhancement of ATF2 transcription (Hikasa et al., 2002; Schambony and Wedlich, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hikasa et al., 2002 and Schambony and Wedlich, 2007.

claim: Wnt8a co-expressed with Ror2 produced a greater than five-fold induction of the ATF2 reporter in Xenopus.
source: Wnt8a co-expressed with Ror2 produced a greater than five-fold induction of the ATF2 reporter in Xenopus (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Co-expression of Wnt5A/Ror2 leads to a similar activation of reporter expression as Wnt8a/Ror2.
source: Co-expression of Wnt5A/Ror2 leads to a similar activation of reporter expression, whereas expressed Ror2 without a co-expressed ligand did not alter expression of the ATF2 reporter.
evidence: The claim is based on reporter assay data described in the text.

claim: Expressed Ror2 without a co-expressed ligand did not alter expression of the ATF2 reporter.
source: Co-expression of Wnt5A/Ror2 leads to a similar activation of reporter expression, whereas expressed Ror2 without a co-expressed ligand did not alter expression of the ATF2 reporter.
evidence: The claim is based on reporter assay data described in the text.

claim: Overexpressing Wnt8a together with dominant-negative Ror23I resulted in a reduction of ATF2 reporter activation compared to Wnt8a/Ror2.
source: We determined whether the kinase domain of Ror2 is required for Wnt8a-dependent activation of the PCP pathway by overexpressing Wnt8a together with dominant-negative Ror23I and observed a reduction of ATF2 reporter activation but an activation of Wnt8a/Ror2.
evidence: The claim is based on reporter assay data described in the text.

claim: Wnt8a serves as a ligand for the receptor Ror2 and induces PCP signaling upon binding.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that Wnt8a serves as a ligand for the receptor Ror2 and induces PCP signaling upon binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ectopic overexpression of Wnt8a modulates cell movements and cell morphology in zebrafish and gene transcription in Xenopus.
source: Thus, ectopic overexpression of Wnt8a modulates cell movements and cell morphology in zebrafish and gene transcription in Xenopus.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The number of filopodia significantly increase from 4 hpf to 6 hpf, which comprises the neural-plate-patterning phase.
source: We found that the number of filopodia significantly increase from in the period from 4 hpf to 6 hpf, which comprises the neural-plate-patterning phase (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The increase in filopodia number from 4 hpf to 6 hpf coincides with increasing Ror2 expression levels during zebrafish development.
source: This coincides with increasing Ror2 expression levels during zebrafish development (Bai et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bai et al., 2014.

claim: Only a modest increase in filopodia number was found when Ror2 was activated, suggesting that Ror2 itself is not rate-limiting.
source: We found only a modest increase in filopodia number when Ror2 was activated, suggesting that Ror2 itself is not rate-limiting (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: When Ror2 function was reduced by overexpression of Ror23I, a significant reduction in filopodia number was observed.
source: However, when Ror2 function was reduced by overexpression of Ror23I, we observed a significant reduction in filopodia number.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data described in the text.

claim: Ror2 signaling is required for filopodia induction of embryonic marginal cells during zebrafish development.
source: We conclude that Ror2 signaling is required for filopodia induction of embryonic marginal cells during zebrafish development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Statistically, more filopodia carrying Wnt8a-GFP clusters on their tips were detected upon Ror2 overexpression within cells.
source: Statistically, more filopodia carrying Wnt8a-GFP clusters on their tips were detected upon Ror2 overexpression within cells (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4E,F.

claim: A significant reduction in the number of cytonemes was found in Ror2-deficient marginal cells.
source: Conversely, we found a significant reduction in the number of cytonemes in Ror2-deficient marginal cells.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data described in the text.

claim: Wnt8a-GFP is still present at the plasma membranes of cells that have compromised Ror2 function, suggesting that intracellular routing of Wnt8a from the producing organelles to the cell membrane is independent of Ror2-dependent cytonemal transport.
source: Wnt8a-GFP is still present at the plasma membranes of cells that have compromised Ror2 function, suggesting that intracellular routing of Wnt8a from the producing organelles to the cell membrane is independent of Ror2-dependent cytonemal transport.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Filopodia without detectable Wnt8a seemed to be unaffected by Ror2 signaling in zebrafish.
source: Filopodia without detectable Wnt8a seemed to be unaffected by Ror2 signaling in zebrafish (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Ror2 has a function in regulating a specific subset of filopodia, those carrying Wnt8a (the Wnt cytonemes), in the zebrafish embryo in vivo.
source: This suggests a function of Ror2 in regulating a specific subset of filopodia, those carrying Wnt8a (the Wnt cytonemes), in the zebrafish embryo in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cytonemes can distribute Wnt8a in a graded manner in the dynamically evolving target tissue.
source: Employing cytonemes as the exclusive transport mechanism from the producing cell group to the target cell group, and assuming an unlimited source of the ligand, we found that cytonemes can distribute Wnt8a in a graded manner in the dynamically evolving target tissue (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Ligand concentration within the morphogenetic field depends on the appearance of the cytonemes.
source: We found that ligand concentration within the morphogenetic field depends on the appearance of the cytonemes (Stanganello et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data and a citation to Stanganello et al., 2015.

claim: Increasing the number of cytonemes per cell (by the experimentally determined factor of 1.61) after expression of Ror2 and Wnt8a in the source cells leads to an enhanced ejection (187%) of the ligand into the target tissue when compared to that in the Wnt8a-producing cells.
source: We also found that increasing the number of cytonemes per cell (by the experimentally determined factor of 1.61) after expression of Ror2 and Wnt8a in the source cells leads to an enhanced ejection (187%) of the ligand into the target tissue when compared to that in the Wnt8a-producing cells (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: By using the measured cytoneme parameters after blockage of Ror2 function (number scaled by 0.388), a decrease to 36% of the Wnt8a concentration compared to the WT situation and a smaller range of the morphogen gradient within the tissue was found.
source: Consistently, by using the measured cytoneme parameters after blockage of Ror2 function (number scaled by 0.388), we found a decrease to 36% of the Wnt8a concentration compared to the WT situation and a smaller range of the morphogen gradient within the tissue.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data described in the text.

claim: Ror2 signaling can specifically regulate the number of Wnt-positive cytonemes in vivo and thus represents a cytoneme-specific regulator.
source: These data suggest that Ror2 signaling can specifically regulate the number of Wnt-positive cytonemes in vivo and thus represents a cytoneme-specific regulator.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and simulations presented in the manuscript.

claim: A strong decrease in the range of Wnt signal activation in the neighboring tissue is predicted when Ror2 function is compromised in the Wnt8a source cells.
source: Furthermore, on the basis of the simulations, we predicted a strong decrease in the range of Wnt signal activation in the neighboring tissue when Ror2 function is compromised in the Wnt8a source cells.
evidence: This is a prediction based on simulation data.

claim: Wnt8a-GFP-positive clusters transit in the plasma membrane of the secreting cell.
source: Using a time-lapse analysis, we observed the formation of Wnt8a-GFP-positive clusters, which transit in the plasma membrane of the secreting cell (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Wnt8a co-localizes with Ror2 at the plasma membrane, suggesting Wnt8a-Ror2 cluster induction.
source: Then, Wnt8a co-localizes with Ror2 at the plasma membrane, suggesting Wnt8a-Ror2 cluster induction (Figure 5C) as previously described (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Wnt8a-Ror2 clusters initiate cytoneme formation and decorate the tip of the outgrowing cytoneme.
source: These clusters initiate cytoneme formation and, consequently, they decorate the tip of the outgrowing cytoneme.
evidence: The claim is based on imaging observations described in the text.

claim: The cytoneme contacts the target cell and Wnt8a-Ror2 forms a cluster at the receiving cell.
source: The cytoneme contacts the target cell and Wnt8a-Ror2 forms a cluster at the receiving cell (Figure 5C, Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Within minutes, the Wnt8a-Ror2 cluster is endocytosed into the target cell.
source: Within minutes, this cluster is endocytosed into the target cell.
evidence: The claim is based on imaging observations described in the text.

claim: Cytonemal Wnt8a-mCherry induces Lrp6-GFP cluster formation at the membrane of the target cell.
source: We find that cytonemal Wnt8a-mCherry induces Lrp6-GFP cluster formation at the membrane of the target (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: A Lrp6-GFP cluster was observed at the contact points of Ror2-positive cytonemes.
source: Indeed, we observe a Lrp6-GFP cluster at the contact points of Ror2-positive cytonemes (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The source cell presents Wnt8a by clustering the ligand on Ror2-positive cytonemes.
source: We hypothesized that the source cell presents Wnt8a by clustering the ligand on Ror2-positive cytonemes.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: Ror2 clusters on cytoneme tips to act as a platform to present Wnt8a to the target cell and to induce the Wnt signaling cascade therein.
source: Therefore, we conclude that Ror2 clusters on cytoneme tips to act as a platform to present Wnt8a to the target cell and to induce the Wnt signaling cascade therein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Overexpression of Ror2 by injection of low levels of mRNA did not induce gross morphological changes in zebrafish embryos.
source: Overexpression of Ror2 by injection of low levels of mRNA did not induce gross morphological changes in zebrafish embryos, consistent with our findings that Ror2 without a suitable ligand only mildly impacts PCP-mediated processes (Figure 3A,C,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and references to Figure 3A,C,E.

claim: Overexpression of Wnt8a resulted in a substantial alteration in neural plate patterning, with β-catenin signaling being activated in the entire neural plate, marked by ubiquitous axin2 expression at 6 hpf.
source: Overexpression of Wnt8a resulted in a substantial alteration in neural plate patterning as described above, with β-catenin signaling being activated in the entire neural plate, marked by ubiquitous axin2 expression at 6 hpf (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Posteriorization of the developing nervous system was observed as an anterior shift of the fgf8a-positive midbrain-hindbrain boundary (MHB) at 9 hpf and a loss of the anterior pax6a-positive forebrain at 26 hpf after Wnt8a overexpression.
source: As a consequence, we observed posteriorization of the developing nervous system, observed as an anterior shift of the fgf8a-positive midbrain-hindbrain boundary (MHB) at 9 hpf and a loss of the anterior pax6a-positive forebrain at 26 hpf.
evidence: The claim is based on in situ hybridization data described in the text.

claim: In embryos co-expressing Wnt8a together with Ror2, posteriorization phenotype in the neural plate was still observed, and CE was compromised, as the neural plate does not converge to the midline and the expression domains of fgf8a at the MHB showed a pronounced gap.
source: In embryos co-expressing Wnt8a together with Ror2, we still observed the posteriorization phenotype in the neural plate and, in addition, we found that CE is compromised, as the neural plate does not converge to the midline and, consequently, the expression domains of fgf8a at the MHB showed a pronounced gap.

claim: The intestinal crypt requires a constant supply of Wnt signaling for tissue homeostasis.
source: As the intestinal crypt requires a constant supply of Wnt signaling for tissue homeostasis (Beumer and Clevers, 2016; Kuhnert et al., 2004; Pinto et al., 2003; Sailaja et al., 2016), we asked whether Wnt cytonemes operate in the mouse intestinal crypt.

claim: Subepithelial myofibroblasts provide the major source of physiologically relevant Wnts, which maintain the crypt in vivo.
source: In vivo, subepithelial myofibroblasts provide the major source of physiologically relevant Wnts, which maintain the crypt in vivo (Kabiri et al., 2014; Valenta et al., 2016).

claim: PdgfRα-positive myofibroblasts regulate the intestinal stem-cell niche by Wnts and RSPO3.
source: It has been further demonstrated that these PdgfRα-positive myofibroblasts regulate the intestinal stem-cell niche by Wnts and RSPO3 (Greicius et al., 2018).

claim: Cytonemes are vital for Wnt protein dissemination in vertebrates.

evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

source: Here, we show that Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) autocrine signaling controls the emergence of cytonemes, and that cytonemes subsequently control paracrine Wnt/β-catenin signal activation.
evidence: This is a main finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Cytonemes subsequently control paracrine Wnt/β-catenin signal activation.
source: Here, we show that Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) autocrine signaling controls the emergence of cytonemes, and that cytonemes subsequently control paracrine Wnt/β-catenin signal activation.

claim: Wnt transport by cytonemes and its control via the Ror2 pathway is highly conserved in vertebrates.
source: We show that cytoneme-based Wnt transport operates in diverse processes, including zebrafish development, murine intestinal crypt and human cancer organoids, demonstrating that Wnt transport by cytonemes and its control via the Ror2 pathway is highly conserved in vertebrates.
evidence: This is a main finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Wnt signaling regulates development and tissue homeostasis in multicellular organisms.
source: Wnt signaling regulates development and tissue homeostasis in multicellular organisms (Nusse and Clevers, 2017), including processes such as cell fate specification, cell proliferation, morphogenesis, and maintenance of tissue integrity.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nusse and Clevers, 2017.

claim: Dysregulation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling has been causally linked to multiple diseases, with Wnt signaling being one of the most frequently dysregulated pathways in several cancer types.
source: Dysregulation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling has been causally linked to multiple diseases, with Wnt signaling being one of the most frequently dysregulated pathways in several cancer types (Anastas and Moon, 2013), including colorectal cancers, pancreatic cancer, and gastric cancers (Chiurillo, 2015; Madan and Virshup, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The Wnt signaling network consists of several branches that can be classified according to the receptors involved and the specific signaling cascades that they activate.
source: The Wnt signaling network consists of several branches that can be classified according to the receptors involved and the specific signaling cascades that they activate.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Wnt signaling.

claim: Two major branches of the Wnt signaling network are the β-catenin-dependent pathway and the β-catenin-independent Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway.
source: Two major branches of this network are the β-catenin-dependent pathway and the β-catenin-independent Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway (Niehrs, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Niehrs, 2012.

claim: The β-catenin dependent pathway is triggered by the interaction of Wnt with Frizzled (Fzd) receptors and the co-receptor Lrp6.
source: The β-catenin dependent pathway is triggered by the interaction of Wnt with Frizzled (Fzd) receptors and the co-receptor Lrp6 (Logan and Nusse, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Logan and Nusse, 2004.

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling regulates the expression of target genes such as axin2 and lef1, as well as the expression of tissue-specific genes, and subsequently controls both cell proliferation and tissue patterning.
source: Wnt/β-catenin signaling regulates the expression of target genes such as axin2 and lef1, as well as the expression of tissue-specific genes, and subsequently controls both cell proliferation and tissue patterning.

claim: In the β-catenin-independent Wnt/PCP pathway, Wnt proteins bind to Frizzled and to co-receptors such as the receptor-tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 2 (Ror2) to regulate cytoskeleton organization by actin polymerization and cell polarity.
source: In the β-catenin-independent Wnt/PCP pathway (Yang and Mlodzik, 2015), Wnt proteins bind to Frizzled and to co-receptors such as the receptor-tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 2 (Ror2) to regulate cytoskeleton organization by actin polymerization and cell polarity (Grumolato et al., 2010; Ho et al., 2012; Oishi et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The small GTPases Rho, Rac1, and Cdc42 are regulated to control the formation of filopodia and lamellipodia, as well as cell motility and morphogenetic movements of cells in vertebrates.
source: To this end, the small GTPases Rho, Rac1, and Cdc42 are regulated to control the formation of filopodia and lamellipodia, as well as cell motility and morphogenetic movements of cells in vertebrates.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PCP signaling.

claim: The PCP pathway and β-catenin signaling generally act in a mutually repressive fashion, by competing for similar hub proteins such as the effector protein Dishevelled (Dvl).
source: Although the PCP pathway and β-catenin signaling generally act in a mutually repressive fashion, by competing for similar hub proteins such as the effector protein Dishevelled (Dvl) (van Amerongen and Nusse, 2009), recent evidence suggests that PCP signaling can act — dependent on the context — either in opposition to, in concert with, or independently of β-catenin signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to van Amerongen and Nusse, 2009.

claim: Recent evidence suggests that PCP signaling can act — dependent on the context — either in opposition to, in concert with, or independently of β-catenin signaling.
source: Although the PCP pathway and β-catenin signaling generally act in a mutually repressive fashion, by competing for similar hub proteins such as the effector protein Dishevelled (Dvl) (van Amerongen and Nusse, 2009), recent evidence suggests that PCP signaling can act — dependent on the context — either in opposition to, in concert with, or independently of β-catenin signaling.

source: The production and secretion of Wnt ligands requires lipid modification by the acyltransferase Porcupine (Porcn) followed by binding to Evi/Wls, which serves as a Wnt chaperone and facilitates its transport from the endoplasmic reticulum to the plasma membrane (Bartscherer and Boutros, 2008; Bänziger et al., 2006; Yu et al., 2014).

claim: The dissemination of Wg/Wnt proteins on exovesicles (more specifically on exosomes) is a trafficking route for Wg/Wnt.
source: These trafficking routes include Wg/Wnt protein distribution on the plasma membrane of dividing source cells (Alexandre et al., 2014; Farin et al., 2016) and actively migrating cells (Serralbo and Marcelle, 2014), or the dissemination of Wg/Wnt proteins on exovesicles (Panáková et al., 2005) (more specifically on exosomes [Beckett et al., 2013; Gross et al., 2012; Korkut et al., 2009]).

source: Wg/Wnt proteins and their receptors are also transported on cell protrusions in various tissues.

claim: Lipid-modified Wnt proteins were found at the cell membrane of signaling filopodia — so-called cytonemes — in Xenopus and zebrafish.
source: Lipid-modified Wnt proteins were found at the cell membrane of signaling filopodia — so-called cytonemes — in Xenopus and zebrafish (Holzer et al., 2012; Luz et al., 2014; Stanganello et al., 2015), whereas Fzd receptor proteins can be localized to filopodia in Drosophila and chicken (Huang and Kornberg, 2016; Sagar et al., 2015).

claim: Fzd receptor proteins can be localized to filopodia in Drosophila and chicken.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Huang and Kornberg, 2016 and Sagar et al., 2015.
